h1: The 6 Best Overhead Phone Arms for Desks Under $40, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Overhead Phone Arms for Desks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 overhead phone arms under $40 for top-down video, compared on reach, joint type, clamp size and load rating.
mainKeyword: overhead phone arm for desk under $40
summary: The SMALLRIG 22 inch Magic Arm is the best overhead phone arm under $40, with a 600g rated load and a standard 1/4-20 interface that also takes a small camera or light. The NEEWER 22 inch is the pick for action-camera owners, the LISEN is the simplest phone-only mount, and the Lamicall 38 inch gooseneck gives the most reach.
intro: Overhead phone arms fail in one predictable way: slow sag. You frame a top-down shot of a recipe, a sketch or a repair, and over ten minutes the arm droops until your subject drifts out of view. The cause is rarely the phone weight alone. It is a long arm, a loose joint and a phone in a thick case, all pulling on a mount designed for a lighter load.

This ranking sorts six arms under $40 by how well they resist that droop, how far they reach and how securely they clamp. We reviewed the specifications supplied for each, including arm length, joint style, clamp opening and rated load. Where a listing gives no load figure, we do not guess one.

products.name: SMALLRIG 22" Magic Arm Clamp, Overhead Phone Mount Holder Stand
products.verdict: A 22 inch articulated arm rated to 600g, with a standard 1/4-20 interface and double-ball clamps.
products.description:
The SMALLRIG magic arm is 22 inches long, rated for 600g (21oz), and uses the standard 1/4-20 mounting interface with double-ball clamps at each joint. It costs between $25 and $50.

It wins because the rated load is a number you can plan around, and it is the only mount here that doubles as a camera or light arm. A 600g rating covers a large phone in a case with margin, so the arm resists the slow sag that plagues thinner designs. The 1/4-20 thread means a small camera, a tiny LED or a microphone can take the phone's place later.

Buy it for desk filming with room to grow. Skip it if you want a long, floppy reach.
products.idealFor: Creators who may add a camera or light later.

products.name: NEEWER 22" Magic Arm w Desk C Clamp
products.verdict: A 22 inch magic arm with anti-twist pins and a phone holder that also fits action cameras.
products.description:
The NEEWER is a 22 inch magic arm with a desk C clamp, an anti-twist pin at each mounting interface, and a phone holder that fits devices 2.2 to 3.2 inches wide. It is named as compatible with GoPro and Insta360 action cameras. Budget note: between $25 and $50.

It ranks second because the anti-twist pins stop the head rotating on its thread, a common annoyance on cheap arms. Action-camera compatibility makes it flexible. The holder width of 2.2 to 3.2 inches suits most phones, but a large phone with a thick case may be too wide, and the listing gives no weight rating.

Choose it if you swap between a phone and an action camera. Skip it if you have a big phone in a thick case.
cons: Holder may not fit large phones
products.idealFor: People who swap phone and action camera.
products.skipIf: Your phone is wider than 3.2 inches.

products.name: LISEN Cell Phone Holder, Overhead Phone Mount
products.verdict: A steel overhead phone arm with tension knobs on each joint and a one-touch release clip.
products.description:
The LISEN is a steel overhead phone holder with a bi-directional adjustable base, tension adjustment knobs on every joint and a one-touch release clip. Budget note: under $25.

It ranks third because the per-joint tension knobs let you tighten each joint as the arm ages, which is the real answer to sag. A steel body is sturdy at this price, and the one-touch clip makes phone changes quick. It is built for phones only, so unlike the magic arms it will not take a camera or a light.

Buy it for simple, repeatable phone filming. Skip it if you want a multi-use arm.
products.idealFor: Phone-only overhead filming on a budget.
products.skipIf: You want to add a camera or light.

products.name: Lamicall Nylon Braided Gooseneck Phone Holder, 38" Overall Length
products.verdict: A 38 inch nylon-braided gooseneck with a 360 degree ball swivel clamp joint.
products.description:
This Lamicall gooseneck is 38 inches long with a nylon-braided arm, a 360 degree ball swivel at the phone clamp and a clamp base that opens up to 3.15 inches. Budget note: under $25.

It ranks fourth because it has the longest reach in the group, useful for a deep desk or a wide drawing board. The ball swivel gives fine angle control. The cost of reach is stability: a 38 inch gooseneck is the most likely to sag or wobble, particularly with a heavy phone, so keep the phone light and the arm short.

Choose it if reach matters more than rigidity. Skip it if you film with a big phone and need a locked position.
products.idealFor: Deep desks and wide drawing boards.
products.skipIf: You need a rigid, locked position.

products.name: Evershop Ring Light Overhead Camera Phone Mount
products.verdict: A 10 inch ring light on a 30 inch extendable dual-spring arm, with 30 colour and brightness combinations.
products.description:
The Evershop pairs a 10 inch ring light, with 30 colour and brightness combinations, and a 30 inch extendable dual-spring arm. The desk clamp fits surfaces up to 2.4 inches thick. Budget note: between $25 and $50.

It ranks fifth because the combined light and arm saves buying two products, which helps a first-time creator. The weight of the ring light can overload the arm, so check how it handles your phone, and its tripod-like footprint takes space. A ring light overhead is good for flat lay shots but reflects in glossy subjects.

Buy it for flat lay photos and video with built-in lighting. Skip it if your subject is shiny.
products.idealFor: Flat lay creators wanting light and mount.

products.name: Lamicall Gooseneck Bed Phone Holder, 33.4" Full Adjustable Arm
products.verdict: A 33.4 inch aluminum-magnesium alloy gooseneck for phones from 4 to 7 inches.
products.description:
This Lamicall gooseneck has an aluminum-magnesium alloy core, a 33.4 inch arm and a clamp base that opens up to 2.36 inches. It fits phones from 4 to 7 inches. Budget note: under $25.

It ranks last because it is sold as a bed holder, so it is built for casual viewing instead of precise overhead framing. The alloy core resists sag better than a plain wire gooseneck, and the phone size range is generous. The base opening of 2.36 inches is the narrowest here, and it will not fit a thick desk.

Buy it if you want a sag-resistant gooseneck for a thin table. Skip it if your desk is thick.
products.idealFor: Thin tables and casual overhead use.
products.skipIf: Your desk is thicker than 2.36 inches.

whatMatters.detail: A load rating, such as 600g, tells you what the arm can hold without drooping. A phone in a case can weigh 250g or more, and an added light weighs more. Check for a number, and leave a margin.
Magic arms use friction joints with locking knobs that stay put, while goosenecks bend freely and may sag. For precise overhead framing, locking joints are more reliable.
A long arm covers more desk but amplifies wobble and sag. Choose the shortest arm that frames your subject. A 22 inch arm is usually enough for a desk.
The clamp must fit the thickness of your desk. Openings range from 2.36 to 3.15 inches here. Measure your desk edge, including any lip, before buying.
Holders have a maximum width, such as 3.2 inches. A big phone in a thick case may not fit. Measure the phone with its case on.

faq.a: Not reliably. They are designed for phones, and the phone holders are too small for tablets. A tablet needs a stronger arm and larger holder.
Extending the arm fully and expecting it to stay put. Shorter arms and tightened joints are far more stable than a long reach.

faq.q: Is the SMALLRIG worth it over the LISEN?
faq.a: If you want to use a camera or light later, yes. For phones only, the LISEN is cheaper and has useful tension knobs.
A few minutes. Clamp the base to the desk, tighten the knobs, attach the phone clip and position the phone. Check the desk edge is not too thick.

faq.q: How do I stop the arm sagging?
faq.a: Tighten the joints, keep the arm short, use a lighter phone case and avoid extending a gooseneck to full length.

faq.q: Can I film vertically and horizontally?
faq.a: Yes. Most clips rotate. The ball swivel on the Lamicall makes changing orientation quick.

finalTake: The SMALLRIG 22 inch Magic Arm is the best overhead phone arm under $40, with a 600g load rating and a standard 1/4-20 interface. The NEEWER suits action-camera owners, the LISEN is the neat phone-only option, and the Lamicall 38 inch gooseneck gives the longest reach. Keep the arm short for stability.
